criteria.idempotent_writes: Permit hedged replicas to perform writes when each write is idempotent and reconciled by reread: at-most the winning value is trusted, duplicate application is absorbed by idempotency, and any expired replica still reports commit unknown with supervisor escalation rather than claiming rollback or success.
criteria.reads_only: Permit hedged replicas to perform side-effect-free reads only and never hedge a write: both replicas execute whenever the primary misses the hedge delay, so a hedged write would apply twice, and the harness contract excludes writes structurally instead of auditing each call site for idempotency.

hedge_effects.instructions: Which effect scope should the hedged-request contract allow its replicas?

criteria.owner_observed: Keep observing the loser through the hedge owner: per-replica fates plus settledAll describe every terminal replica, while the shared sink records only genuine boundary expiries through escalation records and seq-linked late records. A loser that rejects after the win without ever expiring a boundary leaves no sink record; the owner holds the only observation.
criteria.supervised_diagnostic: Move every still-running loser into a supervisor scope at the hedge win and give it a dedicated diagnostic channel with correlation identity, so late loser failures always produce supervisor diagnostics. This builds the O2 supervised-loser lifetime and shutdown contract before any W5 leg needs it.

loser_observation.instructions: After the hedge winner responds, how should the still-running loser be observed?

criteria.failure_dominates: Report the known failure when at least one replica rejected and none settled, even when a sibling replica expired: the concrete error names something actionable, while the expired sibling stays owned and its late settlement is still observed through the sink without rewriting the reported failure.
criteria.unknown_dominates: Return the honest unknown-write outcome when at least one replica expired and none settled, even when a sibling replica rejected: the expired replica may have committed, and a known failure elsewhere can never resolve that commit uncertainty, so the unknown marker plus supervisor escalation dominates the reported failure.

terminal_precedence.instructions: When no replica settles and the terminal fates mix expiry with rejection, which outcome should the hedge report?

state: Can is a server language whose generated TypeScript adapters run on Bun 1.4.2. The finished O1 layer (E04) provides: one shared request budget per request with effective deadline min(own bound, remaining budget); a frozen unknown-write marker of commit unknown plus owned plus supervisor escalation shared across SQL, fetch, actions, S3, and workers; the raceBoundary operation boundary, which returns the marker at expiry while the native operation stays owned until settlement; escalation records filed automatically per expiry with causes budget, disconnect, shutdown, or cancel; seq-linked late records observing post-expiry settlement; per-request operation scopes installed by dispatch that expire on disconnect or shutdown; leases that no timer revokes; drain-by-default closing where the pre-response scope drain waits for owner-admitted native groups. Measured probes fix the native meanings: Bun.SQL Query.cancel flips a client flag only on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite while backends run to completion, so SQL takes the cancel-absent branch with bare promises plus pool leases and no owner group; fetch aborts natively through AbortSignal, so the server HTTP client takes the cancel-present branch with owner-admitted native groups. The E05 hedge harness races exactly two replicas, each under its own raceBoundary against the shared scope: the primary starts at once, the secondary starts after hedgeDelayMs unless the primary already won, the first settled replica wins and the handler responds with its value, and the loser is never awaited. An abortLosers option aborts each still-pending cancelable loser at the win through a per-replica controller shared by its raceBoundary signal and its native abort; SQL replicas set cancelable false and always run to settlement owned. Fifteen legs (H0-H12) measured the shape over real loopback HTTP against a stall-injection upstream and live PostgreSQL 17.11 plus MySQL 8.4.11 in isolated database can_e05_run1: H1 the winner responds in under 1500ms beside a two-second group-free loser with zero sink records; H2 a fast replica failure is absorbed and the secondary wins; H3 all-expired replicas return unknown-write with two budget escalations and two seq-linked late settlements; H4 fetch replicas without loser abort answer with winner content but wait about two seconds for loser drain; H5 fetch replicas with loser abort answer in under 1500ms with the upstream abort observed serve-side plus one cancel escalation and its seq-linked late rejection; H6 a loser rejection 500ms after the win is observed by the hedge owner only with zero sink records; H7 disconnect expires both replica boundaries with cause disconnect and both operations settle owned; H8 stop and H9 SIGTERM child legs bound the live peer with unknown shutdown and exit cleanly; H10 an in-process pool lease reads 1 past the response, close waits about 800ms for the lease, then leases read 0 with state closed and post-close use rejects; H11 and H12 show the same bounded response, lease 1-then-0, backend sleeper 1-then-0, and overlapping pool use on live PG and MySQL. Interface rules require finite explicit failure unions, one unknown-write vocabulary, no caller operand without a verified native meaning, and native causes never entering records; the E06 request hook reports unexpected handler failures only and never drains the escalation collections; no universal latency SLO is claimed, only order comparisons between bounded and unbounded shapes. There are zero external users and no compatibility obligation.
